newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Proton to announce Lotus-related news.
newsitem.headline: Proton to announce Lotus-related news.

text.p: Malaysian national carmaker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) is expected to make an announcement on Wednesday related to British sports car maker Lotus Group, a source close to the talks said.
The source said Proton's UK unit was expected to issue a statement at 1430 GMT on Wednesday. "It's definitely related to Lotus," the source told Reuters, not providing any details.
A report in the Asian Wall Street Journal last week said that Proton was in talks to buy 80 percent of Lotus.
On Tuesday, Lotus said it would give details of its plans for a new partner and for the future at a news conference on Wednesday. It did not identify the partner.
Rumours about the likely partner have centered on South Korea's Daewoo Motor Co Ltd, a unit of Daewoo Group, and Proton.
But Daewoo Motor said on Wednesday that it has shelved plans to buy a major stake in Lotus, an automotive engineering firm and maker of luxury sports cars.
Officials at Proton in Kuala Lumpur could not be reached for comment.
Both Proton and Lotus have declined to comment on the AWSJ report which said Proton would pay $84 million for the stake and assume about $21 million in debt.

Last week, Lotus confirmed that Proton had purchased a Lotus car which it was shipping to Malaysia for studies, and said that the Malaysian company "is in the process of developing a technical collaboration with Lotus."

Proton analysts have said a Lotus deal would give the Malaysian automaker the advanced engine technology it had long sought. They noted that Proton has not tapped into the luxury end of the car market.
